idiom_name: Qt QObject behaviour with properties and signals/slots; std::function callbacks otherwise
implementation_notes: With Qt - the dominant C++ UI stack - reusable stateful behaviour is a QObject-derived class: state is exposed through properties and change signals, consumers connect with QObject::connect (type-safe via the function-pointer syntax), and Qt automatically disconnects when either side is destroyed, so the host never schedules or cancels the subscription itself. That framework mechanism replaces a wrapper or inheritance structure: any widget or plain object can observe the same behaviour object without knowing anything about it, the independence the Qt documentation describes for signals and slots. Without Qt the portable form is a helper class or lambda pair composed through std::function callbacks with hand-managed registration and RAII cleanup; neither form has call-order state slots, so lifetime and thread affinity remain explicit, and the Qt form should be kept when Qt is already in the stack rather than rebuilding its meta-object machinery.
pitfalls: QObject has thread affinity: cross-thread connections must be queued and a behaviour object driven from the wrong thread misbehaves at runtime.
A lambda connection needs a context object (usually this) or it outlives its owner - Qt only auto-disconnects when the sender or the context dies.
Signals may still be delivered during destruction after a derived destructor has run; the Qt docs advise explicitly disconnecting such emitters in destructors.
